newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower as funds flush out stops.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower as funds flush out stops.

text.p: COMEX copper plunged lower for the second day running, ending with some of the losses pared, in fragile technical health and funds continuing to sell their long futures positions, brokers and analysts said.

Funds successfully rooted out sell stops at 85.50 cents basis December on COMEX, pushing the market to a low of 84.50 cents. "But everyone was then so short and over-extended, there was no follow through," a broker said.
December settled 1.25 cents off at 85.90 cents. Volume was estimated at 15,000 lots.
Brokers and analysts noted some trade buying which pared potential losses, and expected LME stocks to drop some 2,000 tonnes Friday. COMEX stocks fell 137 short tons to 20,089 short tons Thursday.

"It does not look like the bottom is in yet," said William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch. "The reason why we have not seen more hedge buying is that a lot of customers are looking forward and see there is probably going to be more than ample supply. There is no incentive for them but to retain hand-to-mouth inventory."
"Another danger for the market is that the producers may not be that well hedged," O'Neill added.
